sources.entry: KeeWeb - Cross-platform password manager compatible with KeePass.

summary.one_liner: KeeWeb is a cross-platform password manager that opens and creates KeePass `kdbx` vaults, usable as a desktop app or in a web browser.
summary.what_it_does: KeeWeb opens existing KeePass `kdbx` database files (including those made by KeePass and KeePassXC) or creates new vaults. It runs as a browser app or as a desktop application on Linux, Windows, and macOS. Vaults can be stored as local files or in cloud services named in the README: Dropbox, Google Drive, and Microsoft OneDrive. The README describes KeeWeb as a single HTML file plus an optional service worker for offline use, and says distribution files can be downloaded from the gh-pages branch. It can be self-hosted, with a Docker image (keeweb/keeweb on Docker Hub or ghcr.io/keeweb/keeweb) and a documented Traefik reverse-proxy and Authentik forward-auth setup. The README also includes build instructions for each platform using Grunt or npm.
use_cases: Open and manage existing KeePass kdbx password databases
Run a password manager in the web browser
Self-host a password manager with Docker
Store a password vault in Dropbox, Google Drive, or OneDrive
Build a desktop password manager app from source
notable: Compatible with KeePass kdbx files created by KeePass, KeePassXC, and others
Runs as a single HTML file in the browser or as a desktop app
Official Docker images with PUID/PGID and port settings
Documented Traefik and Authentik forward-auth setup for self-hosting
Optional Dropbox support on self-hosted setups
caveats: Building from source requires Node v20.9.0 LTS or newer
Self-hosting with Traefik or Authentik requires significant manual configuration (DNS, certificates, labels)
README notes that signing and cloud features depend on paid certificates and domains for the project; Dropbox setup is referred to an external wiki page
